We all get angry, we all feel wronged, we all resent things. We are just often taught to be steadier, not to be so emotional, that so-and-so should behave in such-and-such a way. So we push the shouting down inside, swallow the tears back into the throat, and package it all as maturity with reason. Being good is not another word for being gentle; it is a shape that someone expects you to be tamed into. I don't want to be good any more. I don't want to keep meeting anyone's expectations. I want to allow myself to have feelings, to be weak, to be clumsy sometimes. I want to learn honesty inside my mistakes, instead of losing myself inside a perfection someone else defined. I don't want to be good any more. Not out of rebellion, and not to hurt anyone. It is just that I finally understand that looking after other people does not mean giving yourself up. I can be kind without always giving way. I can be understanding without swallowing the hurt. If the world around me gets a little messy because of that, then let it be messy. At least this time, this is the shape I chose for myself.

叮咚叮咚！聖誕節來啦！當清晨的第一聲鈴鐺響起，一場充滿歡笑、驚喜與溫暖的聖誕小旅: Ding-dong, ding-dong — Christmas is here! When the first bell rings in the morning, a small Christmas trip full of laughter, surprises and warmth quietly begins. Opening the window to welcome Christmas, hanging bright baubles on the tree, wrapping a scarf to wander the busy Christmas market; back home, kneading dough together and baking gingerbread, getting the fragrant Christmas dinner ready. As the night deepens you drift into a sweet sleep under soft starlight, then wake to a Christmas morning of presents and surprises. 《聖誕，叮咚叮咚》 is six original Christmas songs written by Next Door Sound Weavers for children and the whole family: one complete festive day, threading together the moments everyone waits for. The music blends light acoustic pop, warm folk, playful rhythm and gentle lullaby. Christmas is not only bright lights, good food and the presents you waited for; it is decorating together, sharing laughter, and the happiness of keeping each other company. May these six songs have children clapping and singing along, and leave the whole family with a warm Christmas memory. This Christmas — ding-dong, ding-dong! Let's spend it together.
可能是水豚隔比悠趴在門邊，聽見電梯停靠便悄悄抬起頭；柔音牙蜷在熟悉的軟墊裡，耳朵: Maybe Gebiyou the capybara is lying by the door and quietly lifts its head when it hears the lift stop; Rouyinya is curled up on a familiar soft mat, its ears catching every footstep that comes nearer in the corridor; Miyinwan watches the city lights come on from the window; and Linyinwan, while no one is looking, fiddles with a scrap of paper and makes a little rustle in the quiet room. 在松果街，聖誕節有一個溫柔的習慣——為需要陪伴的人，留一盞燈。冬雪悄悄落下，街角: On Pinecone Street, Christmas keeps one gentle habit: leave a light on for anyone who needs company. The winter snow falls quietly, and the first Christmas light on the corner comes on. A little squirrel, A-Li, starts getting a special present ready: a small wooden star made by hand. Then an accident knocks a corner off the star, and A-Li loses the courage to give it away. It is not until Christmas Eve, when Uncle Bear opens his door for him, that A-Li finds out that real warmth does not have to be traded for a perfect present. 《為你留一盞燈：松果街的聖誕》 weaves piano, acoustic guitar, mandolin, marimba, woodwinds, accordion, handbells and all kinds of bright Christmas bells into a winter journey full of childlike play, warmth and laughter. From the light going on at the corner, a handmade present, hot cocoa and a chase after a red ribbon, to Christmas dinner, a starlight dance, and a bright morning full of birdsong, the eight pieces string together a story about taking people in, sharing and love. When Christmas Eve has passed, A-Li has also learned to light a lamp for the next friend who needs company. Because the most precious gift of Christmas is perhaps not what we receive, but that someone is willing to keep a place for us, so the warmth keeps passing on.

For them, this is probably the most important moment of the day.

指彈尼龍吉他的溫潤、毛氈鋼琴細微的機械聲響、低音提琴沉穩而不壓迫的脈動，以及偶爾: The warmth of a fingerstyle nylon-string guitar, the faint mechanical noise of a felt piano, the steady, unhurried pulse of a double bass, and the soft percussion that falls now and then, like small lamps slowly coming on in a room. 這是一封來自隔壁小鎮的冬季情書。透過 21 首單曲，細膩地記錄了情侶男孩與女孩一: This is a winter love letter from the town next door. Through 21 tracks it records, in fine detail, an ordinary and warm winter routine of a couple, the boy and the girl. There are four protagonists: besides the couple, the lively rabbit Rouyinya and the quiet, healing capybara Gebiyou. It runs from the morning light of the cabin out into the town's festivities, and the everyday and the festival weave together into the most moving warmth. This album is a sound poem about the layers of feeling in winter. Its core idea is to catch the contrast and the fusion between the cold outer world of ice and snow and the warmth rising inside. The music becomes a healing "warmth prescription" for the mind. The music begins with a quiet, unhurried faint beat, using extremely soft slow beats and deep bass to draw the slow gathering of feeling and the settling of the mind. The tempo gradually quickens with the story, passing into the gorgeous waltzes of the Christmas and New Year climaxes, and finally finds a steady anchor in the faint beat that keeps going. To guide the listener through the thread of this warm journey, the album's 21 tracks are arranged in five chapters of feeling: I. A prelude of love beneath the cold night: on a cold, snowy night the boy and the girl meet in the cabin, and the story opens with a morning embrace and a shared breakfast. II. The hearty afterglow of the ice and snow world: chasing and playing freely with Rouyinya in the ice and snow, then resting by the fire after the joy outdoors. III. Low-frequency resonance anchoring the mind: feeling slow time together with Gebiyou. The couple bathe and read together, and in the low-frequency resonance body, mind and spirit are cleansed and feeling settles. IV. A Christmas beat woven from warm light: a visit to the market in the town next door, the festive mood woven from warm light, and a grand Christmas dinner that brings love to its fullness. V. A final chapter of echoing resonance at the year's end: on New Year's Eve the feelings of the four protagonists reach their highest point in the countdown, and a gentle waltz sets the full stop at the end of the winter routine. This is not only music; it is a tender freeze-frame of warmth in the cold winter.
